data.name: Krushana
data.gender_notes: Krushana is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Krush’, meaning to delight or to please. The name Krushana is a variation of Krishna, the eighth avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, who is known for his mischievous yet loving demeanor and his delight in his devotees. The name Krushana carries the meaning “Krishna's delight” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Krushana usually hope their child will grow to embody krishna's delight and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Krushana represents the divine aspect of love, compassion, and strength. He is a deity who embodies the qualities of a true leader and warrior, and is revered for his ability to bring peace and happiness to those around him.
data.etymology: Krushana belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Krishna's delight.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Krushana total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Krushana is a Hindu name rooted in Indian history and mythology, symbolizing the love, joy, and mischievousness found in Hindu culture. This name has been passed down through generations, connecting individuals to a rich and diverse heritage. The character of Krishna, whose name this derived, has left a lasting impact on Indian art, literature, and philosophy for over 2,000 years.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Krushana offers more than just a historical connection to the Hindu faith, it is also a reminder of the spiritual importance of joy and love. Embodying the qualities of Krishna, the name is a call to bring happiness and positive energy to those around us. It serves as a reminder of the divine presence within us, encouraging us to act with love and delight in the world around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Krushna signifies the all-attracting and compassionate aspect of God in Hinduism. The name embodies the essence of love, protection, and divine grace. It is a reminder that even in the darkest of times, the divine presence always shines like the moon amongst the stars.

historical_references.reference: Krushna is a popular name for the Hindu deity Vishnu, particularly in the form of Krishna. He is believed to have appeared on earth around 5000 years ago in the Dwapara Yuga, where he played a crucial role in preserving dharma (moral order) by defeating the demon king Kamsa.

Another reference to Krushna is found in the epic Mahabharata, where he is described as the eighth avatar (incarnation) of the god Vishnu, who took birth to protect the Devas (gods) and destroy the demon king Shishupal.
